Consult-first service explanation with calm split hierarchy that maps to cosmetic consults.
Urgent-vs-routine card logic with a visible caveat; helpful for dental triage wording.
Phone/proof artifact and checklist hierarchy for request flow explanation.
Category grid structure maps to check-up, hygiene, urgent, and cosmetic enquiry paths.
Checklist-led assessment hero shows how to make a first-step CTA feel clear.
Trust/alert bar pattern can become a careful regulated review notice without proof overreach.
Dark CTA footer and proof row useful for final enquiry handoff, not logo proof.
Benefit icon row is structurally useful but claim style is a caution reference.
Proof-carousel composition can become source-backed process proof without fake testimonials.
Photo-heavy offer hero is a useful anti-reference for fake clinic or smile imagery.
Dashboard support card is a useful anti-reference for internal app leakage.
Plan comparison grid can inspire appointment-type comparison while avoiding subscription copy.
Centered serif service hero offers quiet typography and visible CTA discipline.
Service solution grid offers scannable cards and link-level CTAs for appointment types.
Icon trio plus artifact layout is useful for explaining patient routing, but its ROI claims are banned.
Regulated proof tiles are directly relevant as a governance stress test and anti-credential warning.
Trust/compliance hero shows alert-bar plus proof-artifact pattern for high-caution categories.
Plain letter-style reassurance is useful for regulated decisions, without copying credentials.
Responsible-claim hero and legal microcopy pattern maps to dental truth boundaries.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Make the first promise route patients to the right safe next action, not to a broad lifestyle claim.
Trust content can sit in calm proof tiles, but only source-backed credentials may appear.
Use non-figurative clinic wayfinding or appointment artifacts until owner-supplied photos are approved.
Credentials, medical authority, and outcome language must be blocked unless directly verified.

bannedUses: Do not copy provider portraits, licensed-provider claims, medical badges, or the Hims brand/voice.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Split the homepage around four patient routes: check-up, hygiene, urgent concern, and cosmetic consult.
Each route card needs title, short eligibility cue, risk note, and one enquiry action.
Primary CTA stays enquiry-led while route cards provide specific secondary actions.
The four-route grid should collapse into thumb-sized stacked decision cards on mobile.

bannedUses: Do not copy treatment categories, product cards, sticky proof strip claims, or health-commerce language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Urgent dental concerns need careful routing language and a caveat that the page is not emergency treatment.
Use plain, low-drama clinical wording that reduces anxiety without making response promises.
The enquiry form should ask appointment type and contact preference, not diagnose symptoms.
Urgent-route labels must be clear without relying on color alone.

bannedUses: Do not copy primary-care claims, prescriptions, emergency guarantees, or medical-condition language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A restrained proof surface can feel premium without heavy shadows or nested cards.
Use subtle layering between proof text, selector, and visual anchor rather than dramatic 3D effects.
If animated, proof panels should advance slowly or only on interaction, never distract from enquiry.
Replace testimonials with verified proof types: service menu, contact path, review-needed note, and source status.

bannedUses: Do not invent customer quotes, portraits, names, employer logos, or satisfaction claims.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A large quiet serif headline can create trust while the body copy stays factual and clinical.
Use centered first-fold hierarchy only if the route picker or CTA remains visible without scrolling on desktop.
Clinic restraint should come from generous vertical rhythm and clear grouping, not empty prestige spacing.
Pair warm clinical white with one sharp action accent and a second muted safety color.

bannedUses: Do not copy Mailchimp preview chrome, discount copy, generic consultancy wording, or the exact hero composition.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use crisp appointment cards with modest radius so the clinic page feels serious, not playful.
Icons should signal route type only: check-up, hygiene, urgent concern, cosmetic consult.
Small abstract appointment artifacts can replace fake clinical photos.
Create tokens for route-card border, caution tint, action accent, and clinical surface.

bannedUses: Do not copy freelancer marketplace search, star ratings, expert names, refund promises, or pro-vetting claims.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: A short guided intake can feel like a calm letter: choose route, add contact, confirm review-needed status.
Use Halifax/North End wording only at area level and avoid address, insurance, or clinic hours unless verified.
A regulated service page can speak plainly and personally without naming fictional staff.
Any title, credential, insurance, or clinical promise stays out until proof is supplied.

bannedUses: Do not copy advisor name, credentials, portrait, fiduciary/legal language, or finance-specific claims.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Enquiry buttons and route cards need active, focus, disabled, and review-required states.
Visible appointment categories should map to truthful page metadata and agent-readable service facts.
Prefer static CSS route artifacts over heavy image galleries until approved clinic media exists.
Legal/review-needed notes must remain readable on mobile, not hidden in tiny footnotes.

bannedUses: Do not copy customer logo strip, AI-reputation claims, product UI screenshot, or signup-with-Google flow.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Photo-led product offer would encourage fake clinic, patient, or smile-result imagery.
Dashboard/app proof leaks internal tooling and does not answer a local patient enquiry decision.
Dark enterprise hero, portrait quote, logos, and percentage proof would create untrue clinic authority.
Useful governance stress test, but doctor-trusted and FDA/pharmacy claims are not available to this fixture.

remixDirection.summary: A regulated, route-picker dental page that feels calm and useful: quiet serif first fold, visible enquiry CTA, four appointment paths, source-backed proof/status ledger, and a no-photo clinical wayfinding artifact.
selectedMoves: Hers/Hims regulated-care structure remixed into safe appointment routing with no borrowed credentials.
Mailchimp quiet service hero typography, rebuilt without builder chrome or generic consultancy copy.
Fiverr/OpenTable card taxonomy converted into four patient decision routes.
Assembly proof surface converted from testimonials into verified-fact and review-needed proof blocks.
Grammarly-style responsible microcopy adapted into readable regulated-category caveats.
explicitRejects: No fake dentists, fake patient photos, clinical interiors, smile results, insurance acceptance, reviews, ratings, emergency guarantees, licensed names, or medical outcomes.
No SaaS logo-strip proof, dashboard screenshots, app-builder chrome, marketplace inventory, or enterprise statistics.
No exact visual copy from any Mobbin reference; all ingredients must be remixed around this fixture business job.
